title: Why Indians? Origins of the tradition
summary: Cahn speculates the tradition began around the turn of the century in black culture, noting Indians were never enslaved; he admits no research exists.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Why the fixation with the Indian? Why an Indian tribe? Why that unit?
You mean, why are the Indians Indians?
Yeah, why? I mean, obviously it's from a black culture.
But why the fixation? Why use an Indian tribe, something which is foreign to their culture, in other words?

Well, we don't really know that it's really foreign, because at the time it started, about approximately 100 years ago, at the turn of the century, as far as I can trace it, there were Indians in and around New Orleans. And the Indians had a little bit more of a little better go of it in Louisiana. They had their own tribes, and they were never an enslaved people. The Indians came to market, brought their produce, and then went back home, whereas the blacks weren't able to do just quite that. That's only an opinion. I have no research on it, because nobody has done any research to find out why there are Indians. They're just there, and they come up with... I do think now the costumes are much more exotic than they had been in the past. I think every year the costumes are getting better and better, which is about the only thing we can say that's handwork that's improving.
